title: Low unemployment masks persistent informality, youth exclusion, weak productivity, child labour, and deteriorating worker rights
source_unit: United Nations Statistics Division, Sustainable Development Goals Report 2026, Goal 8: Decent Work and Economic Growth
geography: Global comparison of economic growth, unemployment, productivity, informality, youth transitions, child labour, and labour rights

denominator.unit: global labour force and economic-output frame

secure_work.value: secure work remains out of reach for many despite historically low unemployment

informal_employment.value: informal employment remains widespread and largely unchanged since 2015

macro_pressures.value: geopolitical tensions, supply-chain disruptions, energy-price volatility, and reduced trade flows weigh on the outlook

observations.method: UN SDG synthesis of global labour-market, economic-growth, employment-status, and macroeconomic indicators.
observations.uncertainty: Unemployment is an incomplete measure of job quality, security, hours, pay, informality, bargaining power, or household welfare; global aggregates conceal regional and subgroup differences.
observations.subgroup: Formal and informal workers, unemployed people, low-income countries, workers exposed to geopolitical and energy shocks, and households dependent on labour income.
observations.counterinterpretation: Low unemployment can provide a platform for wage growth and mobility, while informality may provide income where formal jobs are scarce; neither pattern guarantees decent work or rights.

denominator.unit: global young people and labour-productivity frame

youth_neet.unit: approximately one in five young people globally not in employment, education, or training

productivity_growth.value: labour productivity growth remains below the pre-pandemic 2015-2019 average of 1.8 percent

real_wage_channel.value: insufficient productivity gains constrain the ability to raise real wages and reduce poverty

transition_pressure.value: green, digital, demographic, and geopolitical transitions are changing pathways into work

observations.method: UN SDG compilation of youth NEET, labour-productivity, wage, and transition indicators.
observations.uncertainty: NEET is a broad status measure and does not distinguish caregiving, searching, disability, informal activity, or voluntary choices; productivity is an economy-wide ratio, not an individual wage estimate.
observations.subgroup: Young people, students, caregivers, people with disabilities, new labour-market entrants, low-productivity economies, and workers facing green or digital transition.
observations.counterinterpretation: Some youth outside employment or education engage in unpaid care, informal work, or community activity; transition investments can create new opportunities if access to skills and finance is broad.

denominator.unit: global children of working age and child-labour indicators

child_labour_2024.unit: millions of children affected by child labour

child_labour_change_since_2020.unit: more than millions fewer children affected by child labour since 2020

decent_work_gap.value: progress in reducing child labour coexists with persistent deficits in income security, schooling, protection, and family livelihoods

observations.method: UN SDG synthesis of child-labour estimates and decent-work indicators.
observations.uncertainty: Child-labour estimates depend on survey coverage, definitions, age thresholds, and hidden work; a decline in prevalence does not identify causes or eliminate hazardous conditions.
observations.subgroup: Children, households under income pressure, informal and agricultural workers, schools, employers, and labour-inspection systems.
observations.counterinterpretation: Falling child labour can reflect real progress in schooling, protection, and household security, but shocks and weak enforcement can reverse gains.

observations.period: 2015-2024; freedom of association and collective bargaining

denominator.unit: global labour-rights compliance score, where 0 indicates higher compliance and 10 lower compliance

global_rights_score_2024.unit: global score for freedom of association and collective-bargaining rights in 2024

rights_score_change_since_2015.unit: percent change in the global rights score since 2015, as reported by the assessment

regional_deterioration.value: national compliance with freedom of association and collective-bargaining rights deteriorated in most regions since 2015

institutional_consequence.value: weaker worker rights reduce protection during economic and technological transitions

observations.method: UN SDG review of the labour-rights compliance indicator and regional trends in freedom of association and collective bargaining.
observations.uncertainty: The score is an aggregate rights-compliance measure with a specialized scale; it does not capture every workplace, union, worker, or enforcement experience and does not identify causal drivers.
observations.subgroup: Workers, unions, employers, labour inspectors, informal workers, migrants, and groups facing weaker collective voice.
observations.counterinterpretation: Formal rights may remain usable in some sectors or countries despite global deterioration; collective bargaining can also improve through local organization before national indicators move.

related_sources.claim: ILO Employment and Social Trends 2026 provides complementary labour-market and job-quality estimates.
ILO State of Social Justice 2025 provides complementary rights, informality, and fair-transition analysis.

boundary: This record adds a global decent-work and youth-transition route linking unemployment, informality, productivity, NEET status, child labour, collective bargaining, macro shocks, and transition capacity. It uses aggregate SDG indicators and report synthesis, not individual employment histories, respondent-level attitudes, causal wage estimates, or proof that low unemployment means secure work.

reproduction_audit.retrieval_hash_scope: Official UN SDG 2026 Goal 8 page was reviewed for unemployment, informality, macro pressures, youth NEET, productivity, child labour, and freedom-of-association and collective-bargaining indicators.
